why: The SCOPE of .ci/scripts/quality/check-hook-integrity.sh: which directories under
.claude/hooks/ are audited chains, and which guard files sit outside every chain.
IT LIVES HERE RATHER THAN IN THE GATE BECAUSE THE PORTS ARE COMING. The .claude hook
port turns guards into Python and may add or rename a chain directory. While both
lists were bash arrays inside the gate, every such move was an edit to the enforcement
script itself, by whichever agent happened to be moving files. That is the shape the
gate exists to refuse: the enforcement layer quietly changing its own subject.
THE COST OF GETTING THE CHAIN LIST WRONG IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. post-bash was
absent from the array until 2026-08-28, so cancel-old-ci.sh and refresh-pr-body.sh sat
outside the inventory and could have been deleted with no gate noticing. Before that,
pre-edit and pre-ask were outside it too, and pre-edit/block-inline-python.sh was found
at zero cases in either direction.
NEITHER LIST IS DERIVABLE, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS DECLARED. A chain cannot be found by
globbing for block-*: post-bash holds neither a block-* nor a warn-* file and is still a
real chain. Nor by reading settings.json's wiring: that also wires stop/, context/ and
trapguard/, and the first two are MACHINERY whose absence is LOUD (a missing stop hook
errors on every stop) rather than guards whose absence is SILENT. The admission rule is
whether absence is silent, which is a judgement, so it is written down.
guards_outside_chains carries that same rule for individual files: trapguard/dispatch.py
means traps stop firing, chain-head.sh means both toolchain preconditions go unchecked,
and every one of those is silent. stop/worklist.py and the context/*.py hooks are
deliberately excluded.
The gate REFUSES an empty list on either key. A scope file that scanned to nothing would
turn the whole inventory into a vacuous green, which is the failure this gate is about.
EVERY LIST HERE IS REPO-RELATIVE, WHICH IS THE 2026-09-06 SEAM WIDENING. The gate used
to anchor itself on a single hardcoded .claude/hooks root: chains were bare directory
names inside it, inventory keys were fragments waiting for it to be prepended, and cases
came from exactly one file inside it. A guard that moves OUT of that root does not fail
the gate, it LEAVES the gate -- the corpus shrinks and every assertion still passes over
what is left. That is live today: 47 ported guards are tracked at .claude/rediacc_hooks/
guards/ and the gate cannot see one of them. Repo-relative lists mean a move re-keys one
list in one place, and the gate's logic is never opened to do it.
case_sources is the same seam on the coverage side. While it was one file, moving a
guard's cases into a second suite made that guard read as newly UNCOVERED, and the
cheapest way to clear that red is to baseline the guard, which retires the assertion for
good. Reading every declared source means a case that MOVED still counts and only a case
that was DELETED goes red. The gate also derives its section-C harness from this list
rather than naming a file, so a suite that moves takes its floor rule with it.
RE-KEYED 2026-09-06 BY THE W5 P7 CUTOVER, which is the move this file was created
to absorb. The 46 ported guards are Python modules at .claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/
and are what actually runs; .claude/settings.json now names ONE dispatcher command
per chain instead of 38 script paths. So the guards directory joins guard_dirs and
is now the subject of both assertions, which closes the hole this file's own note
above records: '47 ported guards are tracked at .claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/ and
the gate cannot see one of them'.
.claude/hooks/pre-edit and .claude/hooks/pre-ask LEAVE the list because they no
longer exist: every guard they held was ported, and the bash originals were moved
to .claude/rediacc_hooks/oracles/ (see that directory's README). A declared
directory that is not on disk is refused by the gate, deliberately, so this is not
a silent narrowing -- dropping the two names and adding the one is the whole edit.
.claude/hooks/pre-bash LEAVES THE LIST AT W7 P6 for the same reason, one wave later:
block-pathspecless-git-commit.sh is now guards/block_pathspecless_git_commit.py, and
lib/command-scan.sh moved to the oracle tree with it, so the directory itself is gone.
post-bash stays: its two hooks are Python now (cancel_old_ci.py, refresh_pr_body.py)
and the directory still holds them, so the inventory still has a subject there.
THE ORACLE TREE IS DELIBERATELY NOT A GUARD DIR. Nothing runs those files and
nothing registers them; their absence would be caught by the pytest differential,
loudly, rather than by a guard quietly stopping. Adding them here would also be
refused outright: two guard_dirs may not share a final path segment, and the oracle
tree mirrors the chain names.
THREE PACKAGE FILES JOIN guards_outside_chains, by the same admission rule: is the
absence SILENT. dispatch.py, hookio.py and shellscan.py are not guards, but with any
one of them missing `python3 dispatch.py --chain pre-bash` raises on import and exits
1 -- and exit 1 from a PreToolUse hook does NOT refuse the tool call, so all 37
pre-bash guards would stop enforcing while every Bash call still looked clean. That is
the same failure chain-head.sh's header measures for a missing jq and calls 'strictly
worse than having no hooks at all, because no-hooks is at least visible'. The guards
package's own __init__.py needs no entry here: the directory sweep already lists it.
case_sources GREW ON 2026-09-09, and the entries are the D3 port of the harness.
.claude/hooks/test-hooks.sh was 2,774 lines and one `run:` at 537s. It could not be
SHARDED, because check:ci-language-policy freezes a SET of bash files under
.ci and .claude and one more is refused, so it was PORTED to pytest under
.claude/rediacc_hooks/tests/ instead. The files listed here are where the
cases went: hookcases.py is the data corpus, two test modules hold the cases
that need a fixture (a temp git repo, a stubbed gh, a live process) and cannot be data,
and test_hooks_delegates.py holds the folds section C reads.
THE PORT DELIBERATELY KEEPS THE READER'S SPELLING. covmap scans a case source for the
literal `check 2 guards/block_x.py`, so each ported case carries that string verbatim
as its first argument. A port that spelled its cases `case(2, "guards/block_x.py")`
would have presented ZERO cases for all 46 ported guards -- every one of them reading
as newly UNCOVERED, whose cheapest fix is to baseline them, which retires section B
for good. Adding a source here is the whole re-key; the gate's logic is untouched.
BOTH ERAS WERE LISTED WHILE BOTH EXISTED. Double-counting a case is harmless -- section B
only asks whether a guard has at least one case in each direction -- and listing only
one side would have made a case that MOVED read as a case that was DELETED. The bash era
ended when the harness was deleted; its entry went with it, and the port's guard/rc pairs
were diffed against the harness's first and cover a superset of them.
test_hooks_delegates.py IS HERE FOR SECTION C, not for section B: it declares no cases
and the coverage reader finds none in it. What it holds is the FOLD the harness used to
hold -- a sibling selftest's count, admitted only above a floor -- and section C reads a
case source for exactly that. Without this entry the Python arm would have had no subject
and section C would have refused as auditing nothing, one line after the harness left.
